text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. Developers regularly add their code to a shared repository, and every change triggers an automated build. This means the software is compiled and checked without anyone doing it by hand. As part of the same process, the team runs tests automatically to make sure nothing is broken. CI pipelines organize these steps in a clear order, from building to testing to reporting results. The main benefit is catching issues early, before they become big problems. This saves time, reduces stress, and helps teams deliver better software more quickly.
